questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could improve my language skills (in german), get new international friendships and the opportunity to go skiing when there was time off from the studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only thing that takes it down from a 10 was the difficulty of choosing which courses I was allowed to take and to get them approved at my home university.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It was a well-organised orientation session at University of Vienna. I did not have many questions left unanswered after the orientation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They helped me applying to courses and gave a tour of the faculty with a stay at a pub in the end to get to know eachother.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No further comments on this.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it pretty easy. I found an apartment with two other friends that were also going to Vienna for exchange. We used HousingAnywhere and it worked very well! All landlords are approved to rent out their apartments and it's mostly for exchange students and expats. I lived at Herminengasse 3 - a 5-minute walk from the faculty for around 5500 DKK.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You do not get the social aspect of living with others but if you like it quiet sometimes it's nice and you can get a lot out of your money relative to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not use it but heard that it worked well.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of deadlines during the exam period so you need to check your mail often, but otherwise it worked smoothly.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to fill-out mobility online, send a photo for your student-id and register for courses at the host university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus coordinators on-site offered office hours to help with the registration and Louise Diamant at UCPH was also very helpful!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was a hassle and took 3-4 months of sending new courses to get them pre-approved at UCPH and figuring out which courses you can attend at UniWien. In the end it worked out with getting the courses I needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try and get your courses approved early and get some extra courses on that list in case you're not permitted to take those courses. Remember that it will all work out in the end!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was not too low or too high it was just right.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
MA courses: Microeconomics III, Macroeconomics III and Environmental Economics - Micro III was quite hard but if you put in the effort it is a nice course. Macro III and Environ was a bit hard but very good lecturers so it was nice to follow.
BA course: Welfare Economics - pretty easy course after taking Micro I and II at UCPH, can recommend.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is not the same big classes as at UCPH where the Professor talks and then you have a class session after. The prof. is also your class teacher so you have a good opportunity to ask them directly and get guidance. Furthermore, you get points for your final grade by doing assignments and showing up (only some of the courses) - less pressure on the final exam if you do a good job during the semester!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Decision and Game Theory I & II
Macroeconomics for Economics and Finance
Environmental Economics
Welfare Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Decision and Game Theory I & II and Macroeconomics for Economics and Finance since its a "prioriteret valgfag" and it is very easy to pass the courses when you do your homework.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport and food was less expensive than I expected. Get a semesterkarte for the metro for 70-80 EUR and you're good to travel in Vienna during your whole stay! Housing was also cheaper since you can live very close to the city centre for cheaper than in Cph.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend any of this, but the ESN was good at coordinating events (e.g. ESN Alps, their ski-trip to Mölltaler Gletshcer)

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports and different pub-related activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Ski-trip and going out with the other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a wine hike in the mountains outside of Vienna, go see all the amazing architecture, go to Schwedenplatz for a pub-crawl and go skiing!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. Very similar to Copenhagen but the bike lanes are weird.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to your classmates. It is the only time where you're together with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like the Austrian culture in general. Pretty similar to the Danish culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Give the classes an effort during the semester to get an easy final exam.
Rent a swapfiets to get-around easy.
Don't have all of your friends visit - then you won't have that much time to socialise with locals and other exchange students during your stay.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting better at german and trying to live in another culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exam period. The professors dont plan the exam dates so I had 3 exams 3 days in a row.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: None I can think of.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
